name: Sanballat (the Horonite)
title: Hostile opponent of the rebuilding of Jerusalem
summary: Sanballat was governor of Samaria and one of the leading opponents of Nehemiah and the Jews' work to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. He used mockery, threats, and intrigue to stop the construction project, representing the persistent resistance against God's people being restored after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Mocks the rebuilding effort
keyEvents.description: Sanballat and Tobiah mocked the Jews' attempt to rebuild the wall, ridiculing their weakness and the quality of their work.

keyEvents.title: Plans an attack on Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: As the wall neared completion, Sanballat conspired with other enemies to attack Jerusalem and create confusion.

keyEvents.title: Attempts to lure Nehemiah into a trap
keyEvents.description: Sanballat and Geshem repeatedly sent messengers to Nehemiah inviting him to a meeting on the plain of Ono, but Nehemiah saw through their evil intentions.

keyEvents.title: Sends threatening letters
keyEvents.description: Sanballat sent an open letter with false accusations that Nehemiah was planning a revolt against the Persian king.

keyEvents.title: The Wall Completed Despite Opposition
keyEvents.description: Despite Sanballat's persistent opposition, the wall of Jerusalem was completed in just 52 days, to the shame of their enemies.
